title: Herdr executor B: the verdict comes from durable evidence, never from herdr
description:
The verdict about a worker's work comes from DURABLE EVIDENCE and never from
the substrate. One guarantee, one test, mechanically checkable.

Phase 1 established it and ticks' own collect package is the proof it holds:
collect.go:108-109 says "an error means the check could not be performed ...
never 'the worker failed', which is a verdict", verdicts come only from git and
the result file (:164-175), and the package makes ZERO herdr calls. That last
part is what makes it true by construction rather than by discipline.

The herdr executor must inherit exactly that. Its CollectDetail decides from:
- the report file on disk,
- the commits on the attempt branch,
- the exit/settlement evidence the executor itself recorded,

and from nothing herdr says. herdr answers "is the agent alive", never "did the
work succeed".

This is also what makes a herdr upgrade survivable: a rendering change, a
renamed status word or a dropped connection can cost a dispatch, but it can
never corrupt a result.

THE TEST THAT SETTLES IT: a fixture in which every herdr call returns an error,
driven through a completed attempt, asserting that collect still produces the
correct verdict from the report and the branch. If that test passes, the
guarantee holds; if it cannot be written, the seam is wrong.

Builds on tick 3gv (the five operations).
acceptance_criteria: CollectDetail derives its verdict only from the report file, the branch commits and the executor's own settlement record; a fixture in which EVERY herdr call returns an error still collects the correct verdict for a completed attempt, and is the test of record for this tick; no herdr response can change a verdict, shown by that test rather than argued in prose; go test -short -timeout 45m ./... green (make test-short).
